ModelSelectorKind.description:
Kind of selector a caller supplied. Dynamic aliases are factual only when
the authenticated provider catalog advertised that exact spelling.

This is the one wire contract for `selector_kind`: every producer
serializes the canonical `snake_case` spelling, and every consumer —
catalog projection, `router model` diagnostics and the wrapper's typed
catalog rows — reads through [`Self::from_wire`]. Router once emitted
`provider_advertised_exact_id` for live z.ai rows while the wrapper's
derived parser accepted only the canonical names, so one such row made
`router with` reject the whole catalog (issue #620). A spelling this
build does not know is `Unknown`, never a parse failure: an older wrapper
must degrade to "no alias evidence", not to "no models".

ModelTruthDescriptor.description:

that Router may fill the field from a nearby selector.

ModelAccessPolicy.description:
Model authority attached to one router-issued credential.

An empty allow-list preserves the historical unpinned behavior. A
non-empty list contains every exact selector the holder may request;
multiple entries therefore represent an explicit switching grant.

allow_substitution.description:
Permit a provider to serve a different concrete model than requested.
This never widens `allowed_models` at request time.

substitution_source.description: User-controlled setting that enabled substitution, when enabled.

TokenRecord.description:
One persisted token record.

`id` is the JWT `sub` (a UUID); the JWT itself is NOT stored — only the
metadata required to list/expire/revoke.

account.description: Optional account identifier the token is bound to (multi-account mode).

client_kind.description: Canonical managed client adapter; absent on legacy/manual tokens.

ephemeral.description:
Whether this credential belongs only to a wrapper run.

Dead ephemeral records are compacted as part of the next issuance so
repeated `router with` runs cannot grow durable storage forever.

github_repos.description:
Repositories this token may reach through the GitHub proxy; empty is
unrestricted (issue #262).

`serde(default)` so a store written before this field keeps loading,
and an existing token keeps the access it was issued with.

max_requests.description:
Optional cap on the number of upstream requests this token may make.
`None` means unlimited. Used to bound how much a task can consume.

max_tokens.description:
Optional cap on tokens reported by successful upstream responses.
`None` means unlimited.

model_policy.description:
Exact model authority attached to this credential. Empty is the
backwards-compatible unpinned policy used by manually issued tokens.

rate_limit_per_minute.description: Optional fixed-window request rate limit. `None` means unlimited.

rate_window_requests.description: Requests admitted during the current rate-limit window.

rate_window_started_at.description: Unix timestamp at which the current rate-limit window began.

reserved_tokens.description:
Tokens reserved by requests that have been admitted but have not yet
reported their actual usage.

A hard `max_tokens` cap cannot be enforced from `used_tokens` alone:
usage is only known *after* a response completes, so a single large
answer could push the persisted total arbitrarily far past the cap
(issue #195). Admission therefore reserves the request's declared output
budget up front and counts it against the cap; settlement swaps the
reservation for the real figure. Requests still in flight after a crash
leave a stale reservation, which [`TokenStore::release_stale_reservations`]
clears.

run_lease_expires_at.description:
Expiry of the wrapper process's renewable liveness lease.

`None` is deliberately not treated as live: records written before run
leases existed cannot prove whether their wrapper still exists.

scope.description:
Privilege scope carried by the token. Empty (the default) means an
ordinary client token that may only proxy inference; `"admin"` marks a
credential that also unlocks the administrative endpoints. See
[`crate::token::ADMIN_SCOPE`].

sliding_window_seconds.description:
How long, in seconds, an active token's expiry slides ahead of now.

`None` is a fixed clock: the expiry set at issue time is final, which
is what every token did before. `Some(window)` means a request served
with this token pushes `expires_at` to `now + window`, so a session in
continuous use never expires while one abandoned for longer than the
window still does -- which is the behaviour the bound is for. A
day-long session died mid-work against the fixed 24-hour clock twice
(issue #354).

used_requests.description: Number of upstream requests already made with this token.

used_tokens.description: Total input and output tokens reported for this credential.

TokenRecord.title: TokenRecord

ttl_hours.description: Requested lifetime in hours; clamped by the claim.

model_cooldowns.description: Per-model cooldowns across the pool, where only one model was limited.

paused_accounts.description: Accounts paused by an operator or by `ACCOUNT_PAUSE_AT_PERCENT`.

contributors.description:

reset_times.description:
Distinct provider reset times when pooled accounts disagree. In that
case `resets_at` stays absent rather than inventing one timestamp.

label.description: Label the token was issued with (empty when none was given).

requests.description: Requests authorised for this token since the router started.
